summary: Onboarding 1-1 between sales manager Chris Klevan and newly hired closer Richard Claessen, the day before Richard takes his first calls. They cover the SOPs and Sales Success Hub, the CRM/Close and SalesKick tooling, why a booked call had not zapped through to the closer, and how setters colour-code and confirm bookings. Chris describes the prospect population (95% men, mid-30s to 60s, wanting fat loss, mobility and getting out of pain), the three-pillar pitch (training and mobility, nutrition, lifelong success), and coaches Richard on pitch language and engagement checks. They set a recurring Tue/Thu 12:30 1-1 and confirm the Mon/Wed/Fri 13:00 team meeting.
notable: Confirmation texts to prospects are sent by an AI bot, not a human, and Richard was surprised to learn it: 'Looks like this is a bot that does this, this is not a human.' — 'Yeah, yeah, it's all a bot.'
Chris states set-to-show rate is currently ~70% and that Andrew Musial's close rate is 'close to 40%'.
Financing options named for prospects: Klarna, PayPal, 'Payva'; Chris notes 'There are fees associated with them doing a longer payment plan. There's a little interest that adds on.'
Setter identity: Chris states 'Kim is a guy. Kim is a guy.' — relevant to the KFS setter-code mapping used elsewhere in this corpus.
Setter credit policy on direct bookings: the setter who triages and reschedules 'll get credit for the set, basically'.

Richard was hired on a track record of '400K cash and maintained a 35% close rate' and prior work on Chris's 'MOVES method' offer; nominally overflow-only but expected to take live calls the next day.
Chris parted ways with closer Harry Edmonds for inconsistency: 'He'll go a week and close 60%, and then he'll go a week and close 5%.'
Chris is unwell (eczema, facial infection) and unable to cover calls himself, which is why the new hire is being put on live calls immediately.
